name: Mardi Himal
summary: A short, quieter trek in the Annapurna region, east of the main ABC trail, ending near Mardi Himal Base Camp/Viewpoint beneath Machhapuchhre (Fishtail). Only opened for teahouse trekking in 2012, it offers close-up Himalayan views with fewer crowds than ABC or Everest Base Camp, making it a popular beginner-friendly short trek.

best_time_to_visit.primary: March to May (spring) and September to November/December (autumn)
best_time_to_visit.notes: Spring brings blooming rhododendron forests. Autumn/post-monsoon offers the most stable, clear weather and is the main tourist season.

route_from_kathmandu.trailhead: Kande or Dhampus, reached via Pokhara
transport_options: Kathmandu to Pokhara: flight (~25 min) or drive (6-7 hours) via Prithvi Highway
Pokhara to Kande/Dhampus: short 1-1.5 hour drive

difficulty_notes: One of the more beginner-friendly treks in Nepal. 4-7 hours of walking per day depending on route. Involves stone-step ascents and some steep sections closer to High Camp. Suitable for first-time trekkers with basic fitness; no technical climbing skills required to reach High Camp/Viewpoint (going further to base camp involves rockier terrain). No compulsory guide, though recommended, especially in winter or for solo trekkers.
time_required: 4-7 days depending on route and pace; shorter options via Sidhing village or Landruk cut 1-2 days
permit_notes: ACAP is consistently required; some sources note TIMS enforcement can vary by route/checkpoint on Annapurna-area trails, so travelers should confirm current requirements with NTB or a trekking agency before departure.
estimated_cost_usd: approx 420-490 for an all-inclusive guided 5-7 day package (varies by operator)
culture_notes: Trail passes through Gurung villages including Dhampus; less commercially developed than the main Annapurna Base Camp trail.
data_confidence_notes: TIMS enforcement consistency on Annapurna routes is disputed across sources - flagged as another live example of source conflict for eval design.
